latest_findings.claim: At e<=0.9 (N=64, 4 layers, d_model=64, m2 in [0.1, 1], 600 steps, best-of-5 controls), linear decodability of accel_step kept falling in all 3 seeds. Raw layer-4 accel_step R2 was 0.3927/0.3960/0.4361 (seeds 70/71/72), down from 0.557/0.541/0.570 at e<=0.85, and the headroom-normalised margin was 0.284/0.290/0.320. Margins over control stayed well above the bar (0.240/0.246/0.266; controls 0.150-0.170, spread <= 0.014), and accel_step formed at step 100 in every seed. Force was much weaker: margins of 0.103 (layer 2), 0.084 (layer 2, below the 0.1 bar) and 0.144 (layer 1), headroom-normalised 0.12/0.09/0.17. accel_step beat force in every seed, on both raw and normalised margin.
latest_findings.confidence_note: All three predicted conditions held in all 3 seeds by a wide margin (raw R2 is at least 0.08 below the 0.52 cut-off, and normalised margin at least 0.04 below 0.36), so the verdict does not depend on borderline values. Limits: (1) these are 600-step runs and are not converged. val_mse_ratio is still falling (0.14 to 0.12 over steps 500-600) and accel_step margin is still rising by about 0.002-0.005 per 50 steps, so part of the drop from e<=0.85 could be slower convergence on harder data rather than a lower ceiling. (2) Only one data_seed (0) was used. (3) Checkpoints are 50 steps apart, so the step-100 formation step is coarse. (4) The e<=0.85 comparison values come from a separate experiment run under the same config. Over 0.05 of eccentricity, raw R2 fell about 0.13-0.16, steeper than the roughly 0.19 drop seen over 0.10 from e<=0.75 to e<=0.85, which fits a steepening curve. The verdict would change if 3000-step e<=0.9 runs lifted raw R2 back to 0.55 or more, or if a second data_seed gave normalised margins of 0.38 or more.

latest_findings.claim: At d_model=128 (m2 = 0.5, data_seed 0, e <= 0.5, 6000 steps), both N=64 seeds decode force well above control. Seed 22 has R2 0.82669 at layer 4 (control 0.62264, margin 0.204) and seed 23 has 0.81015 at layer 1 (control 0.60228, margin 0.208). Both stay above the same seed's d128 N=128 value at step 6000: seed 22 is 0.108 higher (vs 0.71829) and seed 23 is 0.045 higher (vs 0.7653). Both pairs compare different layers. The gaps are smaller than the d_model=64 gaps (0.143 and 0.072) but have not closed. accel_step does not show the same N=64 advantage: R2 is 0.924-0.927 at layer 1, with normalised margins 0.730 (seed 22) and 0.733 (seed 23), inside the predicted [0.60, 0.88]. Since force stays below accel_step while accel_step is unchanged across N, the steps_per_orbit effect is specific to physical force and not to per-snapshot acceleration.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both seeds meet the expected-if-true criteria: force margin >= 0.1, gap >= 0.04, and normalised accel_step margin inside the band. Both runs completed 6000/6000 steps. Several things limit confidence. (1) Both pairs compare different layers. Seed 22 is N=64 layer 4 vs N=128 layer 1. Seed 23 is N=64 layer 1 vs N=128 layer 3 (from the trajectory's best layer at step 6000). (2) Seed 23's gap of 0.045 is only 0.005 above the 0.04 bar. A same-layer read could push it into the inconclusive (0.02, 0.04) range: at step 5500 the N=128 seed-23 run was at about 0.761 at layer 1. (3) The N=128 references (0.71829 and 0.7653) are the probes_final values quoted in f-20261016-003007-baee, not values re-read here. (4) Seed 23 is compared at matched step, not matched loss. N=64 ends at val_mse_ratio 0.0027-0.0033, and the N=64 force R2 was still rising about 0.002-0.004 per 500 steps at the end. (5) Only two seeds, on one data_seed. The verdict would move to inconclusive if the same-layer layer-1 reads put seed 23's gap below 0.04. It would also move if a matched-val_mse_ratio comparison shrank either gap to 0.02 or less, which would make the deficit a matter of convergence speed rather than a width-independent ceiling.

latest_findings.claim: At d_model=128, N=128, m2 fixed at 0.5 and 6000 steps, final trained force R2 is 0.71829 for seed 22 (layer 1, control 0.6238, margin 0.0945, below the 0.1 bar) and 0.7653 for seed 23 (layer 3, control 0.64065, margin 0.1247, beats control). Raw force R2 is above the d_model=64 N=128 6000-step values of 0.68-0.70, but the controls are also higher. accel_step is decoded much better than force in both seeds: R2 0.96825 at layer 4 for seed 22 (control 0.7588, normalised margin 0.868) and 0.90529 at layer 1 for seed 23 (control 0.69169, normalised margin 0.693). The N=64 minus N=128 force gap is not computed for either seed because the paired d_model=128 N=64 arm (exp-20261015-224303-7f82) has not finished.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both N=128 runs completed all 6000 steps (val_mse_ratio 0.0159 and 0.0133). The hypothesis is about the N=64 minus N=128 gap, and that cannot be judged until the paired N=64 runs (run-20261016-002356-c1d5 and run-20261016-002356-cbfe, still running or pending) finish. The verdict should then be re-analysed from those runs' probes_final. Other limits: (1) force is still rising at step 6000 in both seeds, by about +0.002 to +0.004 margin per 500 steps, so 6000 steps catches it mid-growth. (2) Seed 23's force best layer moved from layer 1 to layer 3 only at the final checkpoint, so any same-layer comparison with N=64 needs per-layer values. (3) accel_step normalised margins (0.868 and 0.693) are both inside the predicted [0.60, 0.88], but seed 22 is close to the top edge. The 'within 0.03 of N=64' part also needs the paired arm. (4) Seed 23's accel_step best-margin layer is layer 1 with R2 0.905, while the max-over-layers trajectory value is 0.957, so the reading depends on the layer. (5) The d_model=128 force controls (0.62-0.64) are above most d_model=64 m2-fixed controls, so cross-width comparisons should use trained R2, not margin. Supported would need both seeds' N=64 force R2 to be at least 0.04 above 0.71829 and 0.7653. Refuted would need both gaps to be at most 0.02.

latest_findings.claim: N=128 seed 23 (m2 fixed at 0.5, data_seed 1) reached a final layer-1 trained force R2 of 0.81915 at step 24000 (control 0.63336, margin 0.186), which is 0.028 below the N=64 value of 0.8467. The trained R2 at step 12000, read as the layer-1 control plus the 0.178 margin, was 0.811, so the run gained only 0.008 from step 12000 to 24000. Force sat flat at 0.811-0.814 from step 9000 to 17000 and then rose by about 0.005 during the low-lr tail. Final accel_step R2 is 0.94462 at layer 3 against control 0.75933 (margin 0.185). On the headroom-normalised margin, accel_step leads force, 0.770 vs 0.507.
latest_findings.confidence_note: The run completed all 24000 of 24000 planned steps. Force stayed at layer 1 at every checkpoint, so every comparison here is same-layer. It also passed the horizon check: 0.811 at step 12000 is within 0.004 of the 12000-step run's 0.8150. The result falls between the two prediction bands. The 'true' band needed a final R2 of at least 0.827 and a gain of at least 0.01; the run got 0.819 and 0.008. The 'false' band needed a final R2 of at most 0.807, or a gain of at most 0.005 with a gap of at least 0.03; the run's gap is 0.028. accel_step's normalised margin of 0.770 falls inside the expected [0.60, 0.85]. Over steps 12000-24000 val_mse_ratio fell about one decade (0.0433 to 0.0041), but force gained only about 0.008 per decade. In the seed-21 rerun arm over the same steps, force gained 0.032 (0.754 to 0.786). So seed 23 looks close to levelling off about 0.02-0.03 below N=64 rather than closing the gap. That reading rests on one seed and gaps of 0.005-0.01, about the size of within-run checkpoint noise. A layer-1 force R2 of 0.827 or more in a longer or replicate run would move this toward supported. Several more seeds levelling off at 0.025-0.04 below their N=64 values would move it toward a small-ceiling refutation.

latest_findings.claim: N=128 seed 21 (m2 fixed at 0.5, data_seed 1, 24000 steps, run completed) ends with trained force R2 0.78595 at layer 1 (control 0.62758 plus margin 0.158). That is 0.044 below the N=64 12000-step reference of 0.8303, but the reference is at layer 2, so the comparison is cross-layer. Read the same way at layer 1, force R2 is about 0.754 at step 12000 (control plus margin 0.126), so it gains about 0.032 from step 12000 to 24000. The final value is inside the expected-if-true band (<= 0.790), but the gain is just above the 0.03 limit and below the 0.04 refutation bar, so the result falls between the bands. accel_step reaches R2 0.947 at layer 4 against control 0.770, a headroom-normalised margin of 0.77 that has been flat since step 1000. Force is still rising slowly (+0.001-0.002 per 1000 steps at the end).
latest_findings.confidence_note: This is one seed, and the run trained all 24000 planned steps. Two of the three pre-registered criteria were met. Final R2 is <= 0.790, and the horizon check passed: the step-12000 value of about 0.754 is within 0.013 of the 12000-step N=128 run's 0.7662. The third criterion, a gain of no more than 0.03, missed by about 0.002. The step-12000 value comes from the layer-1 control plus a trajectory margin rounded to 3 decimals, so the gain is uncertain by about ±0.001. That is not enough to bring it back under 0.03. Because the N=64 reference sits at layer 2, the 0.044 gap is cross-layer, and a same-layer (layer 1) N=64 value could move it either way. The final value of 0.786 is 0.020 above the 12000-step run's endpoint. So for this seed, the end-of-schedule force level is not capped by the 12000-step endpoint. The rise over steps 12000-24000 (about 0.03 over about 1.08 decades of val_mse_ratio, 0.052 to 0.0044) is slowing but has not levelled off. Two things would settle the verdict: a same-layer N=64 reference, and either a 48000-step run or a second seed. A ceiling would show up as force levelling off at or below about 0.79 with the gap staying >= 0.04. Slow convergence would show up as force reaching >= 0.81.

config.expected_if_false: Final layer-1 trained force R2 <= 0.806 (same-layer gap <= 0.02), which would mean N=128 seed 21 converged toward N=64 and the deficit is slow convergence. A gap in (0.02, 0.04) is inconclusive.
config.expected_if_true: Final layer-1 trained force R2 >= 0.826 (gap >= 0.04 vs 0.78595), force beats control (margin >= 0.1), horizon check passes, and headroom-normalised accel_step margin in [0.60, 0.85].
config.hypothesis: Matched-horizon reference for the seed-21 ceiling test. Setup: m2 fixed at 0.5, data_seed 1, N=64, seed 21, 4 layers, d_model=64, e in [0, 0.5], best-of-3 controls, trained to 24000 steps. Prediction: the final trained force R2 at layer 1 (read from probes_final, unrounded) stays at least 0.04 above the same-layer 24000-step N=128 seed-21 value of 0.78595 (run-20261015-221819-33a7). If so, the N=128 force deficit is a lower ceiling and not slow convergence, on a comparison matched in both layer and horizon. The N=64 best-margin layer is also reported, and if it is not layer 1 the best-layer gap is flagged as cross-layer. Intermediate values are read only as same-layer control plus margin, never from the max-over-layers trajectory field. Horizon check: step-12000 layer-1 trained force R2 here must be within 0.03 of the layer-1 value in probes_final of the 12000-step N=64 seed-21 run (run-20261014-054942-67f0); otherwise the result is reported as horizon-confounded. That run's ID is cited as evidence.

experiment.expected_if_true: Final layer-1 trained force R2 >= 0.826 (gap >= 0.04 vs 0.78595), force beats control (margin >= 0.1), horizon check passes, and headroom-normalised accel_step margin in [0.60, 0.85].
